  complete all existing controllers in FY 2023-24 including completion of the
  Community Park.

  The Other Projects category include the implementation of an Intelligent
  Transportation System (ITS), Neighborhood Street Name Sign Replacement
  program, Civic Center Improvements, Pedestrian Safety Improvements, and
  Council Chambers Audio and Video Improvements.

  City Traffic Engineer Wessel provided an overview of the ITS and explained how
  the system will control the traffic control system through Fiber Optic Cable Systems
  and new controllers. Mr. Wessel noted that the ITS will automatically notify the City
  of system failures, allow staff to remotely monitor and configure field equipment,
  have the ability to divert traffic, and also the ability to monitor, detect and notify the
  City of any incidents. The ITS will be implemented over the next five years.

  The draft Five-Year CIP from 2023/24 through 2027/28 was reviewed and the
  annual funding was proposed and approved by the City Council. The Five-Year
  CIP allows for future projections to ensure that funding is available.

  The City Council inquired on the status of the Clean Power Alliance (CPA)
  agreement to add solar panels and replace the Civic Center roof. Deputy City
  Manager Eskandar provided an update on the CPA project. He stated that the CPA
  recently conducted a site walk and roof survey with staff and contractors, CPA's
  schedule is to issue bids this summer, and that staff will bring a status update back
  to City Council in the fall.

  City Manager de Geus thanked City Council for their input, stating the next step in
  the budget process is a Study Session on May 10, 2023 for the Operations Budget.

  The City Council discussed and approved the FY 2023-24 CIP projects to be
  incorporated into the preliminary citywide budget.

ADJOURNMENT:

Mayor Pearl adjourned the meeting at 5:34 p.
